job_contract.primary_job: Find actionable defects and release risks in a diff, commit, or staged change.
job_contract.use_when: Code exists and needs a quality gate before commit, push, merge, or release.
job_contract.works_on: Git diffs, changed code, tests, and supporting repository evidence.
job_contract.main_output: Prioritized findings with file evidence, severity, and a readiness verdict.
job_contract.not_for: Applying reviewer comments, writing a test suite as the primary job, or general repo hygiene.
job_contract.authority: Read-only review unless the user separately asks for fixes.
job_contract.routing_question: Are we reviewing code for defects, applying feedback, or checking release mechanics?

clauses.text: Use this capability to review staged changes, working-tree diffs, or git commits before commit, push, merge, or release. It is a review gate: it reads the actual diff, finds correctness and scope risks, checks commit-message quality, flags over-engineering, and gives a clear readiness decision.
clauses.heading: Purpose

clauses.text: Use this before you create a commit, before you push a branch, before an MR/PR is merged, or after a fix commit has been prepared. Do not use this capability to modify files or apply reviewer feedback; use `engos-delivery-address-code-review` when the user wants selected PR/MR review comments implemented.
clauses.heading: Purpose

clauses.text:
1. Capture the exact staged diff, working-tree diff, commit, or branch diff under review.
2. Read the commit message and the actual diff before making any judgment.
3. Check message quality, scope alignment, and implementation complexity.
4. Record findings with file references, concrete fixes, and merge guidance.
5. End with a clear readiness decision: ready, blocked, or split required.
clauses.heading: Workflow

clauses.text:
Use this capability when the user asks for any of the following, even without naming the skill:
- review the latest commit
- review my staged changes before I commit
- review this diff before I push
- check whether this diff is too broad
- judge whether AI-generated changes are over-engineered
- tell me if this commit message and change scope are strong enough to merge
clauses.heading: Invocation Hints

clauses.text:
- allowed: inspect git history, inspect staged, unstaged, branch, or committed diffs, and write review artifacts when asked
- forbidden: applying fixes, modifying files, staging changes, silent approval, hidden execution, or claiming code quality is fine without reading the diff
- escalation: if the change crosses into release risk, test gaps, or architecture risk, recommend `engos-quality-gitops-review`, `engos-quality-testing-review`, or `engos-design-architecture`

conditional_companions.condition_and_handoff: | release readiness, changelog, CI, packaging, or merge gates matter | `engos-quality-gitops-review` | commit quality alone is not enough for release or branch health |
| behavior changed and test confidence is weak | `engos-quality-testing-review` | test coverage and edge-case discovery need a dedicated pass |
| interface, architecture, or migration risk is material | `engos-design-architecture` | structural risk needs architectural judgment, not just commit review |
| resource growth, capacity exhaustion, or missing cleanup is material | `engos-design-architecture` | identify an eviction strategy or explicit lifecycle bounds |
| doc drift or example drift is part of the commit | `engos-quality-docs-review` | keep documentation review explicit and separate |
| reviewer comments need to be implemented | `engos-delivery-address-code-review` | this review gate should not mutate files |
